newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Markets sleepwalk to close.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Markets sleepwalk to close.

text.p: Asian debt markets sleep-walked their way to Friday's close, and are likely to be just as quiet next week, with a U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and a handover holiday in Hong Kong dampening activity.
However, a flurry of 144a issues was seen or is expected despite the three-day closure of the Hong Kong market.
A unit of Indonesian pulp and paper company Indah Kiat has launched a US$600 million 144a bond maturing in 2007.
The 10 percent bonds can be called after five years and were priced at 99.347 to yield 10.105 percent, or 362.5 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
Bankers said the issue, increased from an original size of US$500 million, was well received.
Hyundai Motors reportedly priced a US$125 million 10-year seven-year put bond on Thursday in the U.S. 144a market to yield 115 basis points over Treasuries.
Hong Kong syndicate managers expect a unit of Hong Kong-listed Road King Infrastructure Ltd to price its US$100 million 144a issue in New York later Friday.
The 10-year bond is callable in year seven and is expected to price at around 312.5 basis points over the benchmark.
Peregrine Fixed Income is sole lead manager of the issue which on Friday received a BB long-term rating from Standard & Poor's, which also rated Road King Infrastructure BB.
Salomon Brothers is seen launching Quezon Power's US$203 million 20-year bond on Monday, before the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting committee meets.
The FOMC meets on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"We will see very little action in the market with the FOMC meeting," said one syndicate manager.
A Reuter poll taken last week found that 35 of 36 U.S. economists surveyed did not expect the Fed to raise rates at its July meeting. One economist said he was undecided.
A three-day holiday to celebrate Hong Kong's handover to China should also slow activity in the Asian debt markets, as most Asian syndications are arranged here.
"I'd be very surprised to see any deals (next week)," said a senior banker active in the Hong Kong dollar market.
Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Blue chip Hutchison Whampoa Ltd marked one of the last days of British rule by signing a record HK$12.0 billion five-year loan facility which was increased from HK$10 billion.

Bankers said China Construction Holdings' US$60 million note that was launched earlier this week was attracting interest from investors that did not get a piece of the bank's more generously priced issue launched in January.
China Resources Holdings has mandated five banks to arrange a US$250 million five-year loan facility.
The amortising loan pays an interest rate of 40 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate, and the all-in is expected to be less than 50 basis points, bankers said.
In other news, bankers said Korea's Central Banking Corp was raising US$30 million in a one-year floating-rate certificate of deposit in a club deal arranged by Sumitomo Finance Asia.
